Docs/Domain randomization

Domain randomization

Use opt-in procedural variation for training or diagnostics while preserving a clear evaluation definition.

Choose the variation for your experiment

The reference scene-transfer track uses three fixed native kitchens. Procedural table textures, background surfaces and lighting are separate training or diagnostic options. State which variations the policy saw during training and keep the held-out evaluation scenes and checkpoint-selection rule explicit.

The research RandomizedTableSceneBuilder has inert defaults: variation is enabled per axis. It supports appearance changes and optional table-height variation; it does not automatically update the placement of task-added objects.

Enable appearance variation in a task

Research checkout required

The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces.

Inside the research task's scene-loading method, the builder can be configured as follows:

from task.scene_builders import RandomizedTableSceneBuilder

def _load_scene(self, options):
    self.table_scene = RandomizedTableSceneBuilder(
        env=self,
        random_table_texture=True,
        random_background=True,
        random_lighting=True,
    )
    self.table_scene.build()

Keep image observations enabled when studying visual robustness. Record the enabled axes, their parameter ranges, texture library and random seeds. Source references are task/scene_builders/ and docs/howto_randomize_scene.md in the research checkout.

Handle height and camera changes deliberately

If you enable random_table_height, use self.table_scene.table_top_offsets during episode initialization to shift every table-supported task actor consistently. The builder moves the table; it does not move bottles, tools or other task objects for you. Check contacts and success conditions after the geometry change.

Cameras are owned by the task, not the scene builder. Any camera-pose jitter must be configured through the camera path and recorded separately. Keep evaluation at the defined fixed camera profile if you are reporting the native-scene track.

Check that the experiment still measures its intended change

Inspect several seeds and camera views, verify objects remain on their support surfaces, and check that task reset and success conditions still work. Compare appearance-only variation with geometry changes separately when interpreting outcomes.

Report a custom randomization study with its own configuration and results. Use Scene evaluation for the standard three-kitchen protocol and Configurations for the fixed timing, controller and action contract.
